artifacts.summary: All five plan phases completed: a new lean-challenge-observe.sh post-task observer produces the Lean Challenge snapshot at plan-time (resting_status planned) and runs --check at the implement-side statuses, registered in manifest.json's observers block; the design record and plan-compliance.md record every ruling; two now-false header comments in lean-challenge-snapshot.sh were corrected; the derived index-entries.json line_count was reconciled.

completion_data.completion_summary: Wired the Lean Challenge snapshot to a new post-task observer (lean-challenge-observe.sh) that produces the snapshot at plan-time (resting_status planned) and consumes --check at the implement-side statuses, replacing the never-invoked plan-format.md expectation with a real, registered call site. Extended both regression suites (29 and 41 passing cases respectively), recorded every ruling the originating change request asked for in the design record and plan-compliance.md, corrected two now-false header comments in lean-challenge-snapshot.sh (comment-only), and reconciled the derived index-entries.json line count.

memory_candidates.content: This agent system has two distinct extension dispatch seams for 'run something after a phase's status lands': (1) a manifest's top-level `hooks` object, whose `postflight` stage is effectively dead on the /orchestrate path because orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh never sets the TASK_TYPE global skill_run_extension_hook reads; and (2) a manifest's `observers` object (resolved by routing_resolve_observers() in manifest-routing-lib.sh, invoked by run-task-observers.sh from orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's completion path), which receives the correctly-resolved local task_type and a freshly-read resting_status, is prefix-aware, resolve-ALL, timeout-bounded, and advisory/non-blocking by written contract. For 'fire extension-local logic keyed on task_type and/or resting_status', reach for the observer seam, not a postflight lifecycle hook. Observer schema: manifest.json's `observers.<key>` = {script, task_type?, topic? (at least one required), timeout_seconds? (default 30)}. check-extension-docs.sh's Rule X additionally requires the observer's key name or script basename to appear in the extension's own README.md, or it fail()s even though the manifest entry is structurally valid.

verify-touched.sh / run-all.sh always execute the DEPLOYED (.claude/scripts/) copy of a suite, never the source-store copy directly, even when invoked with a source-store path as the touched-path argument. If deploy-headless.sh was last run before a subsequent source-store edit, the verification result silently reflects stale, pre-edit test content. Always `diff -q` the source-store file against its deployed counterpart (or just re-run deploy-headless.sh) immediately before trusting a verify-touched.sh/check-extension-docs.sh result as evidence for work just completed.

sapience_notes.subject: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --force INCIDENT warning
sapience_notes.value: The loud INCIDENT warning text is printed only when --force bypasses the STATUS gate (a task past 'planned'). A --force-bypassed overwrite of an existing manifest while status is still 'planned' (the separate manifest-exists refusal) succeeds silently -- rc 0, no warning text -- even though it is also an exit-73 refusal site being bypassed.

sapience_notes.subject: manifest.json observers block schema and validation
sapience_notes.value: An observer entry is {script, task_type?, topic? (>=1 required), timeout_seconds? (default 30)}. check-extension-docs.sh Rule X additionally fail()s if the observer's key name or script basename is not mentioned anywhere in the declaring extension's own README.md, independent of the manifest's own structural validity.

sapience_notes.subject: run-task-observers.sh script resolution and CWD contract
sapience_notes.value: An observer script is resolved by basename against PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/ (never the manifest-declared path directly), and is invoked with whatever CWD run-task-observers.sh itself inherited -- it never cd's. A registered observer therefore implicitly assumes its caller runs from the repo root that owns specs/.

sapience_notes.subject: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check exit 71 scope
sapience_notes.value: Exit 71 in --check mode covers two distinct cases: no manifest found at the expected path, and a pinned trust-anchor commit that is unreadable from the target project's git history. The design record's exit-code table previously named only the identifier-set-mismatch meaning, which was narrower than the code's actual behavior.

sapience_notes.subject: lean Challenge --check promotion decision
sapience_notes.value: Promoting the --check drift verdict from advisory to blocking was declined, on two grounds: a known false-ambiguity defect in the check (task 462, unlanded) is an unmet precondition, and the design record's own 'evidence from real runs' promotion test has no evidence yet since this task gave the check its first-ever real call site.

sapience_notes.subject: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh and test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh concurrency flakiness
sapience_notes.value: Both suites can fail under heavy concurrent /orchestrate multi-task batch load -- one via a 600s per-suite TIMEOUT, the other via a pure wall-clock timing comparison (case q: a nested-guard elapsed-time check). Both passed cleanly (17/17 and 29/29 respectively) when re-run in isolation moments later. Neither failure correlated with any file touched by the work in progress at the time.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh deployed-copy execution
sapience_notes.value: verify-touched.sh and run-all.sh always execute the suite from the DEPLOYED .claude/scripts/tests/ tree, never the source-store copy, regardless of which path form (source-store or deployed) is passed as the touched-path argument. A verification run against stale deployed content is observationally identical to one against fresh content -- both report pass/fail cleanly -- so the deploy-freshness check must be done separately via diff, not inferred from the verification result's own shape.
